entities.name: Battle of Sentinum
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Battle of Sentinum, fought in 295 BCE, was a pivotal clash between the Roman Republic and the combined forces of the Samnites, Etruscans, and Gauls. This critical engagement took place in the heart of Italy, specifically in the region of Sassoferrato. The battle marked a significant turning point in the Third Samnite War, with the Roman legions emerging victorious and solidifying their control over the Italian peninsula. The events of Sentinum would have far-reaching consequences, shaping the course of Roman expansion and the fate of the region.

The battle itself was a testament to the military prowess of the Roman legionnaires, who faced off against a formidable coalition of opponents. Despite being outnumbered, the Romans employed their classic tactics, relying on their discipline and tactical genius to outmaneuver their foes. The outcome was far from certain, with the Samnites and their allies launching a series of fierce counterattacks. However, the Roman lines held, and the enemy was ultimately repelled. The battle was a defining moment in the history of the Roman Republic, marking a major milestone in the rise of Roman dominance.

The legacy of the Battle of Sentinum can be seen in the subsequent rise of Rome as a major power in the ancient world. The Roman Republic would go on to conquer much of Italy, eventually expanding its territories to encompass the entirety of the Mediterranean. The battle also marked a significant turning point in the history of the Samnites, who would eventually be absorbed into the Roman state. The events of Sentinum would have a lasting impact on the region, shaping the course of history for centuries to come.
